approachQuestion.prompt:
Circular inspection totals. For each request (start,length), sum length consecutive cells on a circular array, wrapping at the end. Return answers in request order.

Input: a=[4,1,-2,3], requests [(3,3),(2,4)]. Output: [8,6].

Constraints: 1 ≤ n,q ≤ 200000; 0 ≤ start < n; 1 ≤ length ≤ n; -1000000 ≤ a[i] ≤ 1000000. Totals fit 64 bits.

Which approach handles the complete task correctly and efficiently?

options.text: Build ordinary leading-zero cumulative totals P. If start+length ≤ n use P[start+length]-P[start]; otherwise use P[n]-P[start]+P[start+length-n].
options.feedback: An allowed request makes at most one wrap, so its cells form either one ordinary range or a suffix and a prefix.
For a=[4,1] and (start=0,length=2), this gives zero instead of five.

options.text: Walk length cells for every request and add them using circular indices.
options.feedback: This gives correct results, but repeatedly traverses overlapping candidates. The selected summary reuses their shared work.

feedback.reason: Build ordinary leading-zero cumulative totals P. If start+length ≤ n use P[start+length]-P[start]; otherwise use P[n]-P[start]+P[start+length-n].
details: Build ordinary leading-zero cumulative totals P. If start+length ≤ n use P[start+length]-P[start]; otherwise use P[n]-P[start]+P[start+length-n].
A wrapping request splits into the suffix starting at start and the prefix after wrapping. Their lengths add to the requested length; do not accidentally include a cell twice at the boundary.

“Build ordinary leading-zero cumulative totals P. If start+length ≤ n use P[start+length]-P[start]; otherwise use P[n]-P[start]+P[start+length-n].”: An allowed request makes at most one wrap, so its cells form either one ordinary range or a suffix and a prefix.
“Always use P[(start+length)%n]-P[start].”: For a=[4,1] and (start=0,length=2), this gives zero instead of five.
“Walk length cells for every request and add them using circular indices.”: This gives correct results, but repeatedly traverses overlapping candidates. The selected summary reuses their shared work.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze only the method in the reveal. Choose its tightest worst-case time and worst-case auxiliary-space pair. Use constant-time 64-bit arithmetic. Exclude read-only input and required output; include every described table. All loops are iterative, with no recursive stack or input copies.

options.text: O(n + q) time; O(n) auxiliary space
O(n + q) time; O(1) auxiliary space
O(n log n + q) time; O(n) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: One prefix array supports both nonwrapping and wrapping queries in fixed work.
details: Build n+1 totals once and use at most two subtractions per query. The table occupies O(n).
Use constant-time 64-bit arithmetic. Exclude read-only input and required output; include every described table. All loops are iterative, with no recursive stack or input copies.

Build n+1 prefix totals in O(n) time. Each of q requests uses either one range difference or two differences and one addition, so even a wrapping request costs O(1). Total time is O(n+q). O(nq) describes directly rescanning up to n cells per request, which the revealed method avoids. O(n log n+q) inserts a sorting or logarithmic preprocessing phase that is absent here.

The prefix table retains n+1 64-bit values, so auxiliary space is O(n); query indices and arithmetic temporaries are constant-sized. The O(n+q)-time/O(1)-space choice drops this table. Exclude the read-only array, supplied requests, and q returned answers, but include the separately allocated prefix table.
